theme: Original Lothal sealing descriptions and disputed attachment supports
question: What original excavation evidence links the repeated elephant sealings and related die groups to physical attachments and find contexts?
outcome: A CISI alias join identifies Rao's excavation object 1864 as L-164: Rao interprets its flat cord-marked underside as a jar stopper, whereas Frenez and Tosi tentatively interpret its group as wooden-box sealings. A local versioned ledger preserves 93 source assertions for twelve elephant-cohort objects and four controls. Original descriptions link repeated impressions on L-189, L-190 and L-193. The 65-sealing and 69-of-90 deposit accounts retain separate scopes, and M-895's motif remains unresolved.
challenge: Rao scans lack useful body text layers; flat contact and cords do not uniquely identify a container; original and later authors differ on support type, nail marks and fire cause. Individual excavation-layer joins are missing.
remedy: Frozen bounded page recovery, OCR with visual checks of decisive pages, exact CISI identity joins, separate observation and interpretation fields, D: local-only record storage and 50 passing author checks.
retry_when: Calibrated reverse and edge views distinguish box corners from vessel rims or stoppers in L-164 and the elephant cohort; original field records resolve individual deposit positions; or a specialist determines M-895's remaining motif. Any functional test requires a jointly frozen bench design.
